Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a recipe into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme recipe and deliver a live timeline: Three-Course Dinner for Six: Two Burners, One Oven for 6 people, three courses
Resource limits: one oven, two burners, one cook, courses go out in order.
Everything must be finished by 19:30.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Three-Course Dinner for Six: Two Burners, One Oven

Guests sit down at half past seven. There are two burners, one oven and one cook, so the oven does the braise first and the tart second, and the burners are rarely both free.

Mise en place
Chop the mirepoix, trim the short ribs and measure the stock: forty minutes of knife work before anything goes on the heat.

Main: braised short ribs
Heat the oven to 300°F; give it 20 minutes. Sear the short ribs in a heavy pot over high heat for 12 minutes, turning once. Lift the ribs out, soften the mirepoix in the same pot for 8 minutes, add the wine and reduce it for 5 minutes, then return the ribs with the stock. Braise the ribs, covered, for 3 hours. Rest the pot off the heat for 20 minutes, then skim the fat and reduce the braising liquid for 15 minutes.

Starter: leek and potato soup
Two hours into the braise, sweat the sliced leeks in butter for 10 minutes. Add the potatoes and the stock and simmer for 30 minutes, then blend the soup smooth; 5 minutes. Hold it warm on the back burner until the guests are seated.

Dessert: apple tart
Roll the pastry and line the tin; 15 minutes. Chill the shell in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes and no more than two hours. Slice the apples and arrange them in the shell; 20 minutes. Bake the tart for 45 minutes the moment the ribs leave the oven, while the ribs are resting.

Service
Ladle the soup when everyone is seated; ten minutes at the table. Plate the ribs ten minutes after the soup bowls are cleared, and give the plating five minutes. Let the main course run as long as it runs. The tart goes out twenty minutes after the main plates come back; ten minutes to slice and serve.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "summary": "one paragraph: what is being made, for how many, by when, under what constraints",
  "servesOrScale": "8 people",
  "deadline": "2026-11-26T18:00:00",
  "constraints": ["one oven", "two burners", "two cooks"]
}
```

This is a three-course dinner—leek and potato soup, braised short ribs, and apple tart—for six people, to be completely served by 19:30, with the courses going out in that order. One cook must work with one oven and two burners: the oven handles the short-rib braise before the tart, while the burners support the searing, vegetables, soup, and reductions. The soup must be held warm until seating; the ribs rest for 20 minutes after braising while the tart bakes, then the braising liquid is reduced. Soup is served for 10 minutes once everyone is seated, the ribs are plated 10 minutes after the soup bowls are cleared, and the tart is served 20 minutes after the main plates return. The source text is complete and does not appear truncated.

```json
{
  "summary": "Prepare a three-course dinner of leek and potato soup, braised short ribs, and apple tart for six people, with everything served by 19:30. One cook must use one oven and two burners; the oven must braise the ribs before baking the tart, and the courses must go out in order. The soup must be held warm until seating, the ribs must rest for 20 minutes while the tart bakes, and service follows the specified clearing, plating, and dessert timing.",
  "servesOrScale": "6 people",
  "deadline": "19:30",
  "constraints": [
    "one oven",
    "two burners",
    "one cook",
    "courses served in order",
    "hold soup warm until guests are seated",
    "rest ribs for 20 minutes while the tart bakes",
    "tart starts when the ribs leave the oven"
  ]
}
```

A track is a single sequential line of work, so steps within it cannot overlap; simultaneous work belongs on separate tracks. Each step has exactly one duration kind: fixed, variable, or indefinite, with the fields appropriate to that kind. A start trigger connects a step to the program clock or to another step through one of the supported trigger types, and every step ID must be unique across the entire program. Every task used by a step must have a matching resource constraint, whose `maxConcurrent` limits how many such tasks can run at once. Repeated work belongs on one replicated step rather than copied steps, with `each` for per-instance follow-ups, `all` for a barrier, and `maxInFlight` when a downstream holding area has limited capacity. This dinner has one cook, so the program should also declare a single actor even though the oven, burners, refrigerator, and other equipment have their own limits.

Expected resource constraints:

- `oven`: `maxConcurrent` 1
- `burner`: `maxConcurrent` 2
- `prep`: `maxConcurrent` 1
- `refrigerator`: `maxConcurrent` 1
- `holding`: `maxConcurrent` 1
- `service`: `maxConcurrent` 1

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "Tracks are sequential lines of work; each step has one duration kind; start triggers link steps to the clock or to other steps; stepIds are unique across the whole program; every task needs a matching resourceConstraint; replicated work uses one replicated step with each/all barriers and maxInFlight when needed.",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "oven", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "burner", "maxConcurrent": 2 },
    { "task": "prep", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "refrigerator", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "holding", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "service", "maxConcurrent": 1 }
  ],
  "actors": 1
}
```

Imagine you have to carry out this recipe yourself, in a kitchen where you have: one oven, two burners, one cook, courses go out in order, and everything must be ready at 19:30. You have only the text below. Read all of it.

List every timed activity you would have to perform, in the order the text gives it, with:

- a short kebab-case `stepId` and a human `name`;
- `task`: the resource it occupies while it runs — the oven, a burner, the thermocycler, the PA, the bench, your own hands. Use the same name every time for the same resource;
- how long it takes: exact (`fixed`), a range (`variable`), or "until I decide" (`indefinite`);
- `sourceSpan`: the exact words in the text you took it from, as `{"quote": "...", "occurrence": n}`, where n says which occurrence of those words you mean (1 for the first). Quote the text verbatim — do not paraphrase it;
- `inferred`: `true` for a step the text never states but the work needs anyway (preheating, thawing, resting, cooling, labelling, sound-check), with `"sourceSpan": null`. Keep these few and obvious.

Split anything the text bundles into one sentence when the parts occupy different resources or different stretches of time ("brown the meat, then simmer for 40 minutes" is two activities). Do not decide yet which activities can overlap, which track they belong to, or what waits for what.

Reply with the step list as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json

  "steps": [
```

Turn 4 of 4 — relationships, then the program.

Take the step list from turn 3 exactly as it stands.

**First, tracks.** Put each step in a track: one track per parallel line of work — per dish, per station, per instrument, per performer, per sample group. Steps in one track run one after another and must not overlap; anything that runs while something else runs belongs in its own track.

**Second, triggers.** Give every step a `startTrigger` from this vocabulary and no other:

- `{"type":"programStart"}` — at t = 0.
- `{"type":"programStartOffset","offsetSeconds":n}` — n seconds after the start; this is how a short track is delayed so it finishes with the others.
- `{"type":"afterStep","stepId":"x"}` — when x ends. Add `"offsetSeconds"` for a gap, `"event":"start"` to hang off x's start instead of its end, `"instances"` when x is replicated.
- `{"type":"afterStepWithBuffer","stepId":"x","bufferSeconds":n}` — n seconds after x ends.
- `{"type":"manual"}` — the person taps to start it: a gate that no clock can predict (guests seated, dough looks right, the surgeon is ready).
- `{"type":"compound","logic":"all"|"any","triggers":[...]}` — wait for all of, or the first of, several triggers.

**Third, refine the question before you answer it.** Within the scope of scheduling these activities for one person to follow, suggest a better version of the question "which activities depend on which, and which can run at the same time?" — one that would expose dependencies this text implies but does not state: things that must cool, rest, preheat, thaw, proof, be held warm, or be ready at the same moment as something else. Write your improved question out, answer it, and revise the triggers accordingly. A step the improved question reveals is added here, marked `"inferred": true`.

**Then emit the complete program JSON** in a single ```json fenced block: `schemaVersion`, `programId`, `name`, `environmentType`, `actors`, `tracks`, and a `resourceConstraints` entry for every `task` any step uses. Carry turn 3's provenance onto each step as `"metadata": {"sourceSpan": ..., "inferred": ...}`.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "0.3.0-alpha",
  "programId": "kebab-case-id",
  "name": "Human title",
  "environmentType": "kitchen",
  "actors": 2,
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "turkey",
      "name": "Turkey",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "preheat-oven",
          "name": "Preheat the oven",
          "task": "oven",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 900 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "metadata": { "sourceSpan": null, "inferred": true }
        },
        {
          "stepId": "roast-turkey",
          "name": "Roast the turkey",
          "task": "oven",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 10800 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "preheat-oven" },
          "metadata": { "sourceSpan": { "quote": "Roast the turkey for 3 hours", "occurrence": 1 }, "inferred": false }
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "oven", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "counter", "maxConcurrent": 2 }
  ],
  "metadata": { "serves": "8" }
}
```

Then finish the job with the tools:
1. If the public catalog already covers this (search_public_recipes or cook_recipe), load that instead and stop — its result already has the live URL.
2. Otherwise keep the program you just built; `rhylthyme://guide/authoring` is the cheat-sheet and `rhylthyme://examples/*` are complete programs to pattern-match.
3. Express the limits as constraints, not as copied JSON: the `resourceConstraints`, `replicates`, `instances` and `maxInFlight` you confirmed in turn 2.
4. Run validate_program and fix every error it reports.
5. Run analyze_schedule with finishAt="19:30" to check the makespan, critical path and resource conflicts; adjust offsets so tracks finish together. Its `bindingConstraints` say which limit is actually gating the makespan.
6. Call visualize_schedule and give the user the live URL plus the Gantt/itinerary from the result. Do not describe the schedule in prose.
